headline: Roman has lost 8.6% of his body weight since Sep 5 and has new evening confusion (stove left on). His Oct 19 fall record is disputed, and his bathing needs and fall risk have increased.

items.statement: Weight fell from 82.3 kg (Sep 5) to 79.8 (Oct 1), 77.3 (Oct 28) and 75.2 kg (Nov 24), a loss of 7.1 kg (8.6%). On Nov 24 the dietitian documented poor appetite, skipped breakfasts, and about 50% of day center lunches eaten. The plan is an oral supplement twice daily, weekly weights, and a dental check.
items.verifier_note: Weights, change (-7.1 kg, 8.6%) match the vitals record; the dietitian note supports poor appetite, skipped breakfast, ~50% of lunches, and the plan (supplement twice daily, weekly weights, dental check). The note says 9% but the record gives 8.6%, which is consistent rounding.

items.statement: On Nov 9 his niece Linda reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, including once leaving the stove on. He was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The nurse planned a urinalysis, medication review, and PCP visit that week. The notes I was given contain no results or PCP follow-up after Nov 9.
items.verifier_note: Note supports the Nov 9 report, confusion, stove, orientation, no fever, and plan. But 'niece' Linda is supported only by the Oct 19 note context (not cited here); in this note she is just 'Linda'. The statement about no results or follow-up is consistent with an empty encounters record, but the niece relationship is not in the cited n004 note.

items.statement: The chart has conflicting information about a fall. A nursing note says Roman fell in the kitchen on Oct 19 with a left forearm skin tear and no reported head strike or loss of consciousness. A chart correction dated Oct 20 says that entry was documented on the wrong participant. The Oct 24 PT evaluation still refers to the fall and found slow, unsteady gait, Timed Up and Go 19 seconds, and a recommendation for a walker, home safety evaluation, and bathroom grab bars. The team should verify whether the fall happened.
items.verifier_note: The fall note, the Oct 20 correction saying wrong participant, and the Oct 24 PT evaluation referencing the fall with gait findings, TUG 19 s, and recommendations are all accurately described, and the conflict is flagged for team verification.

items.statement: On Sep 18 the aide gave hands-on help getting out of the tub, and Roman said he had been skipping showers because he fears slipping. On Sep 25 the OT found he needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing, where he was independent at the last review. The OT recommended a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower, and more home care hours for bathing.
items.verifier_note: Both notes match: aide help out of the tub and skipped showers on Sep 18; OT moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing, independent at last review, and the three recommendations on Sep 25.

items.statement: The PT, OT, and dietitian recommendations are not yet documented as completed. These are the walker, home safety evaluation, grab bars, tub bench, handheld shower, added bathing hours, and dental check. PT planned twice-weekly sessions starting around Oct 24.
items.verifier_note: The recommendations are all in the cited notes, and absence of completion documentation is consistent with the notes given. However, the PT note does not say sessions start around Oct 24; it only says 'will see twice weekly' in an evaluation dated Oct 24, so the start date is an inference.

questions_for_team: Did the Oct 19 fall happen? The correction note (n016) conflicts with the PT evaluation (n002), so who will reconcile the chart and confirm the fall-risk status?
Were the urinalysis, medication review, and PCP visit planned on Nov 9 completed, and what did they show about the evening confusion and the stove safety risk?
What is the work-up and follow-up plan for the 8.6% weight loss over about 12 weeks, and has the dental check or supplement started?
Who will confirm that the bathing equipment, added home care hours, and bathroom safety changes are in place?
As part of the Nov 9 medication review, should the team look at the active naproxen alongside clopidogrel, given anemia on his problem list?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters, ED visits, urgent care visits, and hospital admissions in that window, including any for chest pain, dyspnea, COPD/bronchitis exacerbation, or bleeding.
Falls and near-falls review: check incident reports and notes for falls, fall-related injuries, or gait/balance concerns, given osteoarthritis of the knee, chronic back pain, and fibromyalgia.

Medication reconciliation against the active list (metoprolol succinate 100 mg, clopidogrel 75 mg, naproxen sodium 220 mg, nitroglycerin spray, simvastatin 20 mg): identify any starts, stops, dose changes, or new PRN use in the window, and any new prescribers or pharmacy fills not on the list.

Antiplatelet and NSAID safety: review for GI bleeding signs, melena, bruising, or epistaxis while on clopidogrel plus naproxen; check recent hemoglobin/hematocrit given the anemia diagnosis, and whether the team has discussed the combination.
Cardiac symptoms: review chest pain episodes, nitroglycerin use frequency, dyspnea, edema, and exertional tolerance, given ischemic heart disease.
Blood pressure and heart rate trend across the window, including any readings at home or in clinic; check for hypotension, dizziness, or bradycardia on metoprolol.

Respiratory status: review COPD/chronic bronchitis symptoms, rescue inhaler use (note no inhaler is on the active list, so verify whether one is prescribed elsewhere or whether this is a documentation gap), oxygen use, and any sputum or infection episodes.

Glycemic and metabolic review: check most recent HbA1c and glucose values against the prediabetes and metabolic syndrome entries, and weight trend given BMI 30+ and obesity; record weight change over the window.

Pain and function: assess chronic pain scores, analgesic use, sleep disruption, and ADL/IADL status (bathing, dressing, transfers, meal preparation, medication management, driving), noting any decline since last review.

Cognition, mood, and engagement: screen for changes in cognition, depression or anxiety screen results, social isolation signs, and attendance at PACE day center, therapy, or primary care visits in the window; check for any missed or cancelled appointments.

Caregiver and care-plan items: confirm current caregiver or family contact and any change in living situation or supports; verify care-plan goals, due reassessments, outstanding referrals, and any items due before the 2026-11-30 review date.
